subject: Post-call: Model fit & structured-output evals / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Model fit & structured-output evals / next steps

Thanks again for the quick call today, Sarah — really helpful to get a read on the evaluation goals for Acme's Catalog Summarization workflow. Recap below and proposed next steps.

High-level call takeaways
- Primary goal: replace brittle hand-coded heuristics with a model that reliably emits JSON objects conforming to Acme's catalog schema (product_id, title, short_description, attributes[]).
- Bulk latency target: median generation < 350ms for 512-token prompts when running in your dedicated region.
- Quality priority: schema compliance (valid JSON + required fields) > semantic completeness > brevity.
- Concern: past regressions when model updates changed key formatting and field naming (e.g., "short_desc" vs "short_description"). We should guard via evals and regression checks.

Redwood recommendations (initial)
1) Models to try: redwood-7b-instruct-q4 (fast/cheap), redwood-13b-v2 (better instruction fidelity), and open-mistral-7b-instruct (baseline comparison).
2) Inference config: function-calling style prompt wrappers + structured-output scoring. We'll include JSON schema validation in the eval harness and retry with relaxed decoding (temperature 0.2, 3 sampling attempts) on schema failures.
3) Eval artifacts we'll deliver this week: prompt set (attached as eval_prompt_set_v1.jsonl), a small benchmark excerpt (benchmark_results_excerpt.pdf), and a gist showing the schema-driven parsing / retry logic.

Proposed next steps
- Marissa/Dev: deliver the eval prompt set + run 3-model sweep against your small sample (we'll post results to the Drive folder by EOD Thu, Mar 12).
- Sarah: confirm the canonical JSON schema (if different from the one we discussed) and paste a representative product row by Wed, Mar 11.
- Acme & Redwood: schedule a 30m sync next week to review sweep results and pick a candidate for a 1k-record pilot.

Attachments: eval_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (30 prompts), benchmark_results_excerpt.pdf (2 pages)

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & structured-output evals / next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks great. A few quick notes:
- Attached is our canonical schema (pasted below). We use "short_description" and the attributes array must include "color" and "size" when present.
- Representative product row attached (one_table_row.csv) and pasted here: product_id=AC-1002; title=UltraWidget Pro; short_description=High-performance widget for industrial use; attributes={color: black, size: L}.
- Two asks from our side: 1) can you include an automated check to flag when required fields are missing (we'd like a CSV of failures), and 2) can you surface the raw model output for failed rows for triage?

Also, curious about the retry strategy — would it be: if schema validation fails, automatically call the model up to N times with adjusted decoding parameters and finally mark as failed? That would be perfect.

I'll confirm availability for next week once I get the proposed time slots.

Best,
Sarah Jones

sarah.jones@acme.com | +1 (212) 555-9876

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & structured-output evals / next steps

@Sarah — thanks for the schema and sample row. Quick technical note on implementation and the planned eval harness:

Planned schema-validation + retry logic (draft)- Step 0: call model with function-calling / structured-output prompt wrapper (temperature=0.0, top_p=0.95) to prefer deterministic outputs.
- Step 1: validate output against JSON Schema (we'll use AJV in the harness).
- Step 2: if validation fails, run up to 2 retries with adjusted decoding: temperature=0.2, beam-like sampling via top_k=50 for diversity. We capture each attempt's raw output and parsing errors.
- Step 3: if still invalid after retries, classify the row as FAILED and surface the three raw outputs + parse errors to the CSV of failures and to the triage folder in Drive.
- Step 4: for certain classes of error (missing required field but present in text), we also run a targeted regeneration prompt that asks the model to only emit the missing fields in JSON (faster and higher success).

Metrics we'll report in the benchmark excerpt
- Schema pass rate (primary)
- Field-level F1 for extracted attributes (secondary)
- Median token usage and median latency per call

I uploaded a quick prototype of the parser+retry harness as a gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood-evals/abcdef1234567890 — feel free to poke around.

I'll kick off the sweep tonight against the sample and post intermediate results in the Drive folder.

—Dev
Dev Patel

Perfect — thanks Dev and Sarah. A couple clarifications and commitments from Redwood: 

- We'll run the three-model sweep (redwood-7b-instruct-q4, redwood-13b-v2, open-mistral-7b-instruct) on your 200-row sample and share a results summary + raw failure CSV by EOD Thu.
- The failure CSV will include: row_id, attempted_outputs (up to 3), validation_error, model, latency_ms. We'll also mark whether a targeted regeneration succeeded.
- For the demo/poC phase we'll add an automated regression check: when we re-run the same prompt set on a new model version, we'll diff schema pass rates and field-level deltas and surface any >5% regression for review.

Proposed pilot schedule
- Thu, Mar 12: deliver sweep results + failure CSV + Drive folder with artifacts.
- Mon, Mar 16: 30m review call to pick pilot candidate and discuss SLA/latency targets.

Sarah — can you confirm a Mon morning PST slot (10:00-11:00) or Mon afternoon PST (14:00-14:30)? We'll hold both tentatively.
